en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Third Chapter
The Discourse on the Divine Ear:
Is it the case that the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, becomes the divine ear?
Yes, it is.
Is the fleshly ear the divine ear? Is the divine ear the fleshly ear?
One should not say so...
[and so forth] ...Is the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, the divine ear?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is the fleshly ear exactly like the divine ear, and the divine ear exactly like the fleshly ear?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Is it the case that the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, becomes the divine ear? Yes.
Is that very same fleshly ear the divine ear, and that very same divine ear the fleshly ear?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, becomes the divine ear? Yes.
Is the range, power, and domain of the fleshly ear exactly the same as the range, power, and domain of the divine ear?
One should certainly not say so... [etc.
Is it the case that the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, becomes the divine ear?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Having been appropriated, it becomes non-appropriated”?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Having been appropriated, does it become non-appropriated? Yes.
Having been of the sense-sphere, does it become of the fine-material sphere?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Having been a being of the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara), one becomes a being of the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara)? Yes.
"Having been of the fine-material sphere, one becomes of the immaterial sphere"?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
"Having been of the fine-material sphere, one becomes of the immaterial sphere"?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Having been included, does it become unincluded?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, the divine ear?
Yes. Is the divine ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, the fleshly ear? No.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that the fleshly ear, when fortified by the Dhamma, becomes the divine ear?
Yes, it is.
Is there only one stream?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is there only one stream?
“Yes.
“But have not two kinds of hearing been spoken of by the Blessed One—
the fleshly ear and the divine ear?”
“Yes.
“If two kinds of hearing were spoken of by the Blessed One—
the fleshly ear and the divine ear— then indeed, it should not be said [that there is only one].”
“Only one stream.
The discussion on the divine ear is finished.
